title: Cut Zero-Sum Runs From a Chain
statement:
You get the head of a singly linked list of integers. Remove runs of consecutive nodes that add up to 0 until no such run is left, and return the head of what remains (an empty list if nothing remains).

Several different results are often possible, so use this exact rule: walk from the front. At each node, if one or more runs that start at this node sum to 0, delete the longest of them and continue with the node right after it. Otherwise keep the node and move to the next one.

(The rule is what the standard prefix-sum solution produces, and its result never contains a zero-sum run.)

examples.why: At the front, 1 + 2 − 3 = 0, so those three go. −3 + 3 was also zero, but −3 is already gone.
A single 0 is a run of length one that sums to 0.

hints: Keep a running total from the front. What does it mean if the total after node i equals the total after node j?
Equal prefix sums mean everything strictly between them adds up to 0. The longest run starting right after a point ends at the last place the same prefix sum appears.
Pass 1: map each prefix sum to the last node where it occurs. Pass 2: from a dummy node, recompute the prefix sum and link each kept node straight to the node after that last occurrence.

explain.intuition:
Let P be the running sum. A run from node i + 1 to node j sums to 0 exactly when P(i) = P(j). So zero-sum runs are just pairs of equal prefix sums, the same trick as "subarray sums to zero" on arrays.

Put a dummy node with prefix 0 in front. Standing on a kept node with prefix p, the longest zero-sum run that starts right after it ends at the last node whose prefix is also p. So one pass records the last node for each prefix sum, and a second pass rewires node.next to jump past it. After a jump the next node can never start a zero run, because no later node shares that prefix sum.
steps: Pass 1: walk from dummy with a running sum and store last[sum] = node; later nodes overwrite earlier ones.
Pass 2: walk from dummy again with a running sum. At each node set node.next = last[sum].next, then move to node.next.
pitfalls: Forgetting the dummy node. Without prefix 0 before the head, runs that start at the head (like [5, -5]) are missed.
Storing the first node for each prefix sum. You need the last one to cut the longest run.
Deleting one zero run and rescanning from the start each time. That is quadratic on long lists.

solutions.title: Follow the rule literally
solutions.idea: At each position, sum forward and remember the furthest point where the sum hits 0. Skip to there, or keep the node.

solutions.title: Prefix sums, last occurrence
solutions.idea: Map each prefix sum to the last node where it appears, then link every kept node straight past that node.

followups: Do it in one pass with a stack of prefix sums. Which result does that produce on [1, 2, -3, 3, 1], and is it still free of zero-sum runs?
Instead of deleting, return how many nodes would be removed.
lcTitle: Remove Zero Sum Consecutive Nodes from Linked List
